title: Majestic Win: Two Pin-and-Fork Finishes
summary: Place a bishop where capturing it draws the queen onto a knight-fork square. Compare the two king locations before choosing the diagonal.

nodes.question: How can the bishop force a tactical concession?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Qxb5. White has Kg4, Nb7, Bg6 and h6 against Ka6, Qb5 and Na2. The earlier rook and pawn sacrifices are source context.

nodes.question: How does the plan change with the king on b5?
nodes.explanation: This separately pictured seven-piece ending follows ...Kxb5. Black has Kb5 and Qc6, so the bishop must choose a different diagonal.

branches.title: Pin on d3, then fork from c5
commentary: Begin after ...Qxb5. White has Kg4, Nb7, Bg6 and h6 against Ka6, Qb5 and Na2. The earlier rook and pawn sacrifices are source context.
Bd3 pins Qb5 to Ka6 along d3-c4-b5-a6, offering the bishop to the queen.
Qxd3 captures the bishop and removes the pin, but puts the queen on a knight-fork square.
Nc5+ checks Ka6 and attacks Qd3 at the same time.
Kb6 escapes the check in the illustrated reply, leaving the queen attacked.
Nxd3 wins the queen. White retains a tablebase-checked win with the knight and advanced h-pawn against Black’s knight. The further conversion is outside this branch.
branches.explanation: Nxd3 wins the queen. White retains a tablebase-checked win with the knight and advanced h-pawn against Black’s knight. The further conversion is outside this branch.

branches.title: Pin on e8, then fork from d6
commentary: Compare the separately saved ending with the black king on b5.
Be8 pins Qc6 along e8-d7-c6-b5. The new king location requires this different bishop diagonal.
Qxe8 takes the bishop but places the queen where Nd6 will attack it with check.
Nd6+ checks Kb5 and attacks Qe8, buying the tempo needed to recover the queen.
Kc6 is the illustrated flight from the knight check.
Nxe8 captures the queen. The exact knight-and-pawn ending is winning for White; the source’s later compressed king walk is not encoded.
branches.explanation: Nxe8 captures the queen. The exact knight-and-pawn ending is winning for White; the source’s later compressed king walk is not encoded.

exercises.prompt: Why offer a bishop rather than rush h7?
exercises.answer: The bishop pins the queen to its king. Capturing the bishop draws the queen onto d3, where Nc5 checks the king and attacks the queen.
With Kb5 and Qc6, the relevant diagonal is e8-d7-c6-b5. The fork square changes from c5 to d6.

startContext: Two visually reconstructed seven-piece diagrams begin after ...Qxb5 at 69s and ...Kxb5 at 109s. The earlier ten-piece setup, rook sacrifice and eight-piece pawn fork remain source context. These are two selected source capture replies, not a claim that Black must always capture the bishop.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
